central_topic: Empirical prediction of the expected cover time of simple random walks on small connected graphs (n <= 30) from a few cheap graph statistics (n, m, degrees, diameter), compared against classical worst-case cover-time bounds, with per-family error and Monte Carlo uncertainty.
core_methods: log-linear ridge regression of Monte Carlo cover-time estimates on log graph statistics (n, m, mean/max/min degree, diameter, log n * log diameter)
Monte Carlo estimation of uniform-start expected cover time with standard errors
exact maximum hitting time computation for the Matthews reference bound
comparators: Matthews bound: max hitting time times harmonic number
electrical-network / commute-time characterisation of cover time
constant and OLS log-linear reference predictors
benchmarks: programmatically generated graph families: path, cycle, star, complete, 2D grid, binary tree, lollipop, random tree, Erdos-Renyi, random 3-regular (5 <= n <= 30)
architectural_shifts: from worst-case analytic bounds to a data-fitted statistics-only log-linear predictor (the final model beats the best bound in every family; lollipop gain CI touches zero)
result_driven_themes: classical bounds are loosest on dense / expander-like families (complete, Erdos-Renyi, random 3-regular), where cover time scales like n log n
smallest gains on the lollipop family, the extremal n^3 cover/hitting-time construction
grid and complete/ER families have the largest residual log error of the fitted predictor
feature permutation destroys accuracy, so the statistics carry real signal

queries.query: electrical resistance of a graph captures its commute and cover times
queries.rationale: Explains why m, degree and diameter statistics should predict cover time (cover time ~ m * effective resistance up to log n), motivating the feature set.

queries.query: Feige tight lower bound cover time n log n
queries.rationale: The n log n regime of complete, ER and random regular graphs is where bounds are loosest (largest gains); the lower bound literature frames this.

queries.query: cover time of random regular graphs and sparse random graphs Cooper Frieze
queries.rationale: Random 3-regular and Erdos-Renyi families are test families; asymptotic cover-time results contextualise predictor behaviour on them.

queries.query: cover times for Brownian motion and random walks in two dimensions torus
queries.rationale: Grid family has one of the largest residual errors; the 2D cover-time asymptotics (n log^2 n) explain the regime mismatch.

queries.query: maximum hitting time for random walks on graphs lollipop
queries.rationale: Lollipop is the extremal n^3 construction and the family where gains over bounds are smallest (CI includes zero).

queries.rationale: Standard textbook reference for cover time, Matthews method and hitting-time computations used in the evaluation.
